authority: Generated mechanical evidence, never normative project input. PASS validity checks exact identities and reruns state/revision predicates on bound inputs; a JSON PASS string alone is insufficient.
checkedCommit: Null for an uncommitted candidate; acceptance requires an existing commit whose normative state equals the proven state. Unrelated Git changes do not change semantic identity.
revisionBaseline: Accepted baseline commit or null for initial bootstrap; stored provenance for verification, not a substitute for current baseline resolution during candidate evaluation.
bootstrap: Only when no accepted proof exists in canonical history. Invalid/unvalidated canonical state after a prior acceptance is CANONICAL_STATE_INVALID, never a reset to bootstrap.
proofScope: Historical PASS Verification/Validation is retained but applies only to its exact criterion/outcome revision, realization and evidence revisions. UNKNOWN is neither PASS nor FAIL.
historicalBaselineReplay: For explicit canonical revalidation, retain checkedCommit and original revisionBaseline provenance and replay bound state/revision predicates. Historical identity may differ in spec/checker build; it never satisfies current accepted() identity. Replay cannot accept a PASS string without state identity, commit ancestry and revision predicates. FAIL and null-checkedCommit artifacts establish no historical acceptance and do not prevent initial bootstrap.
baselineAcceptanceProvenance: A historical revision baseline must belong to the configured canonical first-parent Git history, not merely be a proof-bearing proposal ancestor. Corroborate positions within the retained native local canonical-ref observation window; pruned or absent reflogs do not replace portable canonical history with cache authority. The validated configuration must designate the selected canonicalRef. A candidate proof is never by itself an accepted-state witness.
